title: Predicted vs actual (out-of-fold)
shows: Every out-of-fold prediction from the 3 time folds (each predicted by a model that never saw its month).
finding: Clean labels hug the diagonal: 69% of loads within ±2%, 98% within ±5%, 100.0% within ±10%. The anomalous labels (right, orange) sit far off the line on both sides; the model predicts a normal price for them, which is the intended behaviour.

title: Size of errors
shows: Left: histogram of signed % error. Right: cumulative share of loads with absolute error below x.
finding: Errors are symmetric and centred near zero (mean +0.33%, median +0.25%). 90th percentile absolute error: 3.4%.

title: Where does the model err?
shows: Grey bars: MAPE per segment. Red line: mean signed % error (bias; + = over-prediction).
finding: Accuracy (MAPE) is similar in every equipment, distance, weight and weekday segment (1.5–1.9%). Bias shows mild structure: short hauls (<250 mi) are under-predicted by 0.5% and the longest hauls over-predicted by 0.8%, a hint that the single distance exponent is slightly too steep at the extremes. The largest structure is by month (-1.0% to +2.0%): the remaining error is mostly about the market level of a period.
decision: Acceptable (all segment biases within ±1%). A possible next step is a distance spline in stage 1. The month-level bias is the main risk for Nov–Dec, hence the trend checks.

title: Error over time
shows: Daily mean signed error and 7-day MAPE across the three evaluation windows (dashed lines = fold boundaries).
finding: Errors grow with distance from the training cut-off. Mean MAPE goes from 1.29% in the first two weeks of a fold to 1.83% in the last two, and the bias drifts by +0.6 / +1.6 / -1.1 points (folds 1/2/3) over the 8 weeks, in a direction that depends on how the market moved. Fold 2 (Jul–Aug) runs high: it was trained on only six months, when the trend was over-estimated (see checks).
decision: Expect late-December predictions to be less accurate than early-November ones (roughly 1.8% vs 1.3% MAPE if the pattern repeats). Retraining weekly or monthly in production would keep the horizon short.

title: Feature importance
shows: Mean absolute contribution of each feature to log(rate) on the training rows: Ridge coefficient × centred feature for stage 1 (teal); exact SHAP values of the LightGBM member of the stage-2 ensemble (gold; the XGBoost and Extra Trees members learn the same residual and are not shown). Log scale.
finding: Distance dominates (moves price by ~52% on average). Then equipment, weight, market index, quarter-end and trend in stage 1. Stage-2 corrections are small (mostly geography: pickup/delivery coordinates), refining the price by a few percent.
decision: Confirms the design: the extrapolating drivers are in stage 1, the tree stage only refines.

title: Learned geographic effects
shows: Average SHAP contribution of the pickup (left) and delivery (right) coordinates, per city, as a % price adjustment.
finding: Smooth regional patterns rather than city-by-city noise, which is what lets the model price cities it has never seen from their location.

title: Do the Nov–Dec predictions join the history sensibly?
shows: Median rate per mile per day: actual training labels, out-of-fold predictions, and the submitted predictions for November–December.
finding: The submitted predictions continue the October level and keep the same weekly rhythm; no jump at 1 November. Validation median $/mile 2.18 vs October actual 2.17.

title: Sanity of the submitted predictions
shows: Left: submitted validation predictions vs training actuals. Right: predicted $/mile by distance and equipment for the 12,000 validation loads.
finding: All 12,000 predictions are positive and finite ($194–$7,001); the distribution matches training, and the distance/equipment structure is preserved for every load including the unseen cities.
